'''Manta''', known formerly as '''Drago''', is a [[Heavyweights|heavyweight]] robot built by [[Team Tanto Robotics]] which has fought at ''[[BattleBots]]'' ''[[BattleBots Proving Ground|Proving Ground]]'' and [[BattleBots FaceOffs|''FaceOffs'']] in 2024 and 2025. It will also take part in the 2026 ''[[BattleBots Pro League|Pro League]]''. It is a four-wheel drive robot armed with a 20" wide, 75lb (originally 70lb) [[Eggbeater Spinners|eggbeater]] [[Drum Spinners|drum spinner]] machined from hardened 4340 alloy steel. The primary weapon is powered by two TP5870 brushless inrunner motors.[https://discord.com/channels/293793025761476611/412189458637520896/1095421859891257416 Public message by Nick Dobrikov in the Out of the Arena Discord server] Manta also sports four large serrated forks at the front, which are hinged to feed opponents into its 12,000rpm spinning drum, which reaches the 250mph tip speed limit. [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-QU7_YUfEpE Drago Battlebots Application 2022] These forks can be swapped out for a wide front wedge if preferred. Team captain Nick Dobrikov has previous experience with [[Malice]] in both the [[World Championship V|2020]] and [[World Championship VI|2021 seasons]] of ''BattleBots'' and has previously designed and built various drum spinners in lower weight classes. Under its original name, Drago was one of two robots to be sponsored by [[Team Malice]] ahead of the seventh reboot season, alongside [[Banshee]].https://www.facebook.com/malicebattlebot/posts/511694550359419 Unlike Banshee, however, Drago was not selected to compete. Drago was renamed '''Drago X''' in 2022 before eventually the team eventually settled on the name '''Manta'''. In a February 2024 interview with ''Green Square Talks BattleBots'', Nick Dobrikov stated he opted to change the name as a result of similarly-named robots such as [[Black Dragon]] and [[Dragon King]], both of which competed in World Championship VII, as well as being unsure what color scheme to give the robot under its original name.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iaXx6nxxqh0 Green Square Talks Battlebots: Proving Grounds Review Part 5 (w/ Manta)] The team applied for World Championship VIII following the conclusion of ''RoboGames'' 2023, which marked the robot's competitive debut.https://discord.com/channels/293793025761476611/412189458637520896/1094773685480587315 Dobrikov dropped the separate self-righter arm seen on the robot's CAD, which was also not present at ''RoboGames'', and gave Manta a blue and grey color scheme to accompany its bright yellow weapon.[https://discord.com/channels/293793025761476611/412189458637520896/1095940672646811698 Public message by Nick Dobrikov in the Out of the Arena Discord server] Manta was scheduled to compete in [[BattleBots Proving Ground|''BattleBots Proving Ground'']] on the weekend of June 24-25, 2023, fighting twice against a robot called [[Magnitude|Atomic Pumpkin]]. However, its opponent withdrew in late May and a replacement had to be found. This ended up being [[Team Overboard]] and [[Triton]], who Manta twice defeated by knockout to end its run unbeaten. In a September 20, 2023 episode of the ''Behind the Bots'' podcast, [[Greg Munson]] revealed Manta was effectively accepted for World Championship VIII, pending the season being green-lit and the team being available to compete.[https://www.podbean.com/ew/pb-eiirr-14ad55d Behind the Bots - ''BattleBots Champions'' II Preview with ''BattleBots'' Co-Creator Greg Munson!] Manta was penciled in to return to the [[BattleBox]] as Nick Dobrikov teased its return, confirming an unknown opponent would be a "dream fight" for him. It was confirmed later in the year that Manta would be competing in ''BattleBots FaceOffs''. Manta weighed 13lbs more than in its ''Proving Ground'' appearances and the drum, which was now machined from a single piece of material rather than having welded teeth, was quoted as weighing 70lbs. Manta breezed through all three of its opponents, winning the [[Giant Washer]] with its 3-0 record. Returning in 2025, Manta fought in the 'BattleBots: Next Generation' ''FaceOffs'' group against [[Banshee]], [[Calypso]] and [[Disarray]]. For this competition, it debuted a brand new alloy steel weapon weighing 75lbs. Manta also competed in the 2026 ''[[BattleBots Pro League]]'' alongside 23 other competitors. Utilizing their spare weight, Manta's team produced thicker ½" AR500 steel side armor to replace their standard ⅜" thick material if needed. The team were accompanied by Banshee team members David Small and Caleb Hecht for the event. Manta_Pro_League.png|Manta during the ''BattleBots Pro League''. Drago.png|CAD of Manta as Drago in 2022. ==Outside BattleBots== Nick Dobrikov regularly competes at ''National Havoc Robot League'' events with '''Noisy Boy''' and has previously entered the 2017 and 2018 editions of ''RoboGames'' with '''Tsunami''' and '''Tsunami Light'''. Tsunami won gold in the junior bracket of its debut ''RoboGames'' campaign, but neither it nor its smaller counterpart would replicate that success a year later. Team Tanto also entered robots called '''Maverick''' and '''Rogue Wave''' into ''RoboGames'' 2017, ending with 6-2 and 0-2 records respectively. As well as this, Dobrikov's team competed in ''Sparkfun AVC'' 2017 with '''Tsunami''', '''Maverick''', as well as a hobbyweight named '''Typhoon'''. With assistance from former [[Team Malice]] member [[Team Small Robots|David Small]], Nick Dobrikov entered the 2023 edition of ''RoboGames'' with '''Manta''', which originally signed up under the name '''Drago X'''. After receiving a bye in the first round, Manta took out [[Big Dill|Banana Runt]] in destructive fashion. Returning for Day 3, Manta lost to veteran [[HexaDecimator]] in the winner's bracket, bursting into flames after being flipped upside-down, despite causing serious damage to [[Team WhoopAss|Team WhoopAss']] robot. After having its internals replaced, Manta almost faced disqualification as the team raced to get their robot ready again. Manta returned to winning ways as it knocked out Ray Billings and [[Hardcore Robotics|Stinkeye]]. It then took the win over ''BattleBots'' World Championship VII alternate [[Terrortops]] in controversial circumstances. Both robots were on the unfortunate end of an arena breach, in which one of Terrortops' forks damaged the Lexan roof and landed outside the arena, mere feet away from the camera crew. Post-fight, Terrortops captain [[Team Terrortops|Ben Burton]] gifted Nick Dobrikov the dislodged fork. Despite the emerging safety issues with the arena, Manta was still eligible to advance in the bracket. It would win its next fight over [[Lucky|Ziggy Jr.]] before facing [[Malice|White Rabbit]] in the Loser's Bracket final. Here, the battle was again stopped when an inner Lexan panel got dislodged and fell from the ceiling, after Manta flung one of White Rabbit's weapon teeth against the roof panel above it. The affected inner panel was removed, and the battle restarted with no repairs being carried out to the arena. Manta continued to inflict damage to White Rabbit, eventually throwing it into the ceiling and dislodging another Lexan roof panel in the process. White Rabbit tapped out immediately, enabling Manta to face [[MadCatter|Cataclysm]] in the overall final. Manta won the first of two potential encounters against [[Team Bad Kitty|Martin Mason's]] machine, damaging it so severely that Mason decided to formally forfeit the rematch. Thus, Manta was declared the overall 2023 ''RoboGames'' heavyweight champion. Alongside [[Banshee]] and [[JackPot]], Manta was on display during the June 2023 Arizona Robot Combat ''RoboRumble'' event.Image provided by Discord user iDontGiveaFett Looking to defend its title, Manta competed at ''RoboGames'' 2024 despite uncertainty on whether they would compete in the heavyweight division, following the safety concerns surrounding the 2023 competition. Manta received a Round 1 bye and took on former champion '''Original Sin''' in the second round of the winner's bracket. After a worrying moment which cost Manta part of its drum, it tore a tire away from [[Team Special Delivery|Gary Gin's]] robot and edged out a pushing match and won by knockout. Manta then dispatched of '''Echo 3.0''' and [[JackPot|BlackJack]] to earn a match against Chad New and [[Magnitude]]. Manta got the better of the [[Team Wazio]] robot and advanced to the finals, where it took on '''Ragin Scotsman''' - winner of the loser's bracket. Manta won the final and earned its second ''RoboGames'' heavyweight championship in as many years. In June 2024, Manta was on display at that year's ''Open Sauce'' event. Later in the year, Nick Dobrikov and Manta featured in a YouTube video by streamer and content creator Kai Cenat.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WIh76o3XDt8 KAI CENAT BATTLE BOTS]  Manta was again exhibited at ''Open Sauce'' 2025. '''Manta vs. Atomic Pumpkin (6/24/2023)'''

Manta's ''BattleBots'' debut was scheduled to come against [[Magnitude|Atomic Pumpkin]], but its opponent withdrew so Manta had to fight a replacement. |- |

'''Manta vs. Triton (6/24/2023)'''

Manta's replacement turned out to be [[Triton]], as announced on June 11, 2023 by ''BattleBots''. For Manta's first fight, it was armed with a wide front plow rather than its forks of various sizes.

[[File:Manta Triton Proving Ground 1.gif|left|thumb|The initial impact.]]In the opening seconds, Triton was struck by Manta and sent twisting and turning through the air. {{Quote|Oh my... oh my... OHHHH!!|Bil Dwyer reacts to the initial impact}}As soon as Triton landed, Manta immediately dealt a follow-up shot which threw Bradley Hanstad's bot towards the screws.

Now smoking and with its blade warped and unable to spin, Triton's vulnerable back end was left exposed and Manta capitalized, biting into its frame. With its left-side drive also compromised[https://discord.com/channels/651601084019900483/809971550937808926/1122615627278975096 Public message from Kaz Church in the NHRL Discord server], Manta's assault continued, throwing Triton into the air again and almost out of the arena completely.

[[File:Triton post Manta Proving Ground.png|thumb|Triton post-fight.]]Manta powered its weapon down and returned to the blue starting square as a count mercifully began on just thirty seconds into the fight. Triton was immobilized and Manta picked up its first ''BattleBots'' win, taking only cosmetic damage. |- |

'''Manta vs. Atomic Pumpkin (6/25/2023)'''

Manta was due to fight [[Magnitude|Atomic Pumpkin]] again that weekend, but due to the aforementioned withdrawal, this fight could not go ahead. |- |

'''Manta vs. Triton (6/25/2023)'''

[[File:Manta Triton Proving Ground.jpg|left|thumb|Triton vs. Manta, as revealed by ''BattleBots''.]]Manta fought [[Triton]] for a second time during the weekend.

Both robots began this fight slightly more tentatively than the day prior, but Manta quickly got its weapon up to speed and struck the side of Triton, propelling it through the air again.
{{Dialogue a-b|Steve Judkins|How's the noise, Bil?!|Bil Dwyer|My goodness!|Steve Judkins and Bil Dwyer react to Manta's 'death hum'}}
[[File:Manta Triton KO 6-25.png|thumb|Triton immobile near the red square.]]These attacks snapped all of Triton's weapon belts, rendering its horizontal spinner useless. One final attack saw Manta get underneath Triton and strike the frame again, and from this moment, Triton was no longer mobile. A count began and Manta won by knockout again, ending the weekend unbeaten. |- ! scope="col" style="text-align: center;" | === BattleBots FaceOffs=== |- |

'''Manta vs. Rusty'''

Manta faced three opponents during ''BattleBots FaceOffs'' in 2024. The first of these was the returning [[Rusty]], which had a single fork fitted to its front in an attempt to get under Manta and cause problems for its weapon if ripped off. Nick Dobrikov's team sported a fork setup of their own - the outermost forks being short while the innermost ones were longer.

[[File:Rusty vs Manta FaceOffs 1.png|left|thumb|Manta removes Rusty's fork in the opening seconds.]]Manta got its drum up to speed in the time it took Rusty to traverse the arena, and tore away Rusty's fork. Manta's 70lb drum grinded against the front of Rusty, causing sparks as [[Steve Judkins]] praised its durable armor. Manta continued to cause damage as it began peeling its opponent's side armor while pushing it towards the left of the [[Upper Deck]].

[[File:Rusty vs Manta FaceOffs 2.png|thumb|Manta carries Rusty across the arena.]]After returning to the middle of the arena, Rusty was allowed to give chase and swung its arm for the first time in the battle. Rusty missed and Manta took advantage, maneuvring to Rusty's side and shoving it towards the teams' booths.

[[File:Rusty vs Manta KO FaceOffs.png|left|thumb|Manta flips Rusty over and leaves it to be counted out.]]Manta struck the axe blade of Rusty as it failed to retract, splitting it down the middle and buckling the arms. This impact also flipped Rusty over, which was hammered by the nearby pulverizer and counted out soon after as it could not right itself. |- |

'''Manta vs. Hellfire'''

Second was [[Hellfire]], which lost its first and only ''Proving Ground'' outing prior to this group. Manta's team equipped the robot with its wide plow for this battle, as seen in both ''Proving Ground'' wins against Triton.

[[File:Hellfire Manta FaceOffs 1.gif|thumb|Manta is flipped over early on.]]Manta quickly approached Hellfire, which remained in its blue starting square as the bots went weapon-to-weapon. Hellfire's undercutter clipped the side of Manta's wedge and overturned it, with the wide wheelbase making it difficult for Nick Dobrikov's team to use gyroscopic forces from its drum spinner to self-right.

[[File:Hellfire Manta FaceOffs 2.gif|left|thumb|Seconds later, Manta is thrown into the corner.]]Hellfire exited its square as Manta settled, but its weapon was less effective while inverted and spinning downward. As Hellfire approached, its bar grazed against Manta's drum before a wild impact sent both robots flailing in different directions. While Manta landed upright, its wedge was caught on debris and a weapon belt had been lost. Meanwhile, its opponent lay dormant over the killsaws, facing away from Manta with a snapped chain laying behind it.

[[File:Hellfire Manta KO FaceOffs.png|thumb|Manta leaves Hellfire for dead.]]A knockout count began against Hellfire and despite a worrying start, Manta's 2-0 record was confirmed. |- |

'''Manta vs. Traves T.'''

[[File:Team Tanto Robotics and Team 2x4 repair Traves T FaceOffs.png|left|thumb|Manta's team help out as Traves T. undergoes repairs.]]Manta lastly took on [[Traves T.]], captained by [[Team 2x4|Kurt Krueger]]. Looking to go 3-0, it was again equipped with the wide front wedge. Ahead of this fight, Manta's team had helped their opponents repair Traves T. after picking up its first win.

[[File:Manta Traves T. KO FaceOffs.gif|thumb|Manta makes short work of its opponent.]]Manta made a conscious effort to dominate the middle of the arena as Traves T. spun in place looking to get its weapon up to speed. As Traves T. struggled to face its opponent, Manta closed in and struck its right side, causing the Michigan machine to twist violently through the air. Though it landed upright, Traves T. showed no signs of life after just one hit.

Manta took the win by knockout once more, sealing a third victory and the Giant Washer for Nick Dobrikov's team. |- |

'''Manta vs. Skorpios'''

Manta's first fight in ''BattleBots Pro League'' was a match with fellow [[Giant Washer]] winner [[Skorpios]]. Team captain Nick Dobrikov explained his desire to prove his worth among the BattleBots elite.

[[File:Manta v Skorpios 1.png|thumb|Manta pops Skorpios into the air.]] As the fight started, Manta cautiously evaded a box rush by Skorpios. As the bots turned to face each other, Manta's wide drum made contact with Skorpios' plow, popping Skorpios into the air. This hit left Skorpios' wedge bent upward.

[[File:SkorpiosvMantakillerblow.gif|left|thumb|Manta deals the killer blow onto Skorpios.]] As the bots re-engaged, Skorpios wheelied over Manta once again, with Manta landing a killer blow to Skorpios' underbelly. This hit left Skorpios immobile with no sign of life. Manta, desiring a longer fight, popped Skorpios into the air from the backside, though Skorpios remained incapacitated.

[[File:Skorpioslaysdead.png|thumb|Skorpios stays unresponsive in the arena.]] [[Alex Watson]] proceeded to count out Skorpios, resulting in a quick 24 second knockout victory for the 2-time Robogames champion. |- |
